name: Dark Madder Blue
lede: Dark Madder Blue is a dim, slate blue-grey, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[madder-blue]], traced to Ridgway's 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A darkened madder blue
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[madder-blue]], whose own name points to the madder plant family of dyes rather than to this grey-blue hue directly [1]. The library dates the swatch to Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate XLIII, and again places it in the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, in the block for grayish blue [1]. Ridgway's plates survive only as scans of an aged, printed chart, so the hex value is an approximation of the original ink, not a measurement of it [1].

The closest named neighbor on file is [[black-coral]], with [[deep-slate-blue]] close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 331 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.39 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is fairly steady across the centuries, rises in the twentieth, and peaks in a small sample of 1930s paintings [2]. Henri-Edmond Cross, Karl Isakson and Pierre Puvis de Chavannes all have it well above the archive's average rate [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
